title: The App Never Showed My Son the Letter He Actually Writes | vitalii.no
description:
A first-grader can't read his own handwriting from an app that only ever showed him the printed shape.

In a sans-serif print font the lowercase 'l' is a bare stick, indistinguishable from a capital 'I' and barely different from 'i' — but the letter my first-grader forms in his skrivebok is a slanted loop. The same gap runs through e, t, f, r and a. A child taught only the printed shape can't read his own notebook, and the learning app never showed him what he actually writes.

I shipped Playwrite NO, an open-licensed Norwegian handwriting font engineered from research on norsk stavskrift, self-hosted locally because the kids' devices block Google's font CDN. Every letter lesson now gains a 'this is how we write it by hand' step, plus a printed-to-handwritten matching drill. On the TV kiosk wall, any card for a grade-2-or-under child — letters, words, digits, sums — now renders in the handwriting model, and it earned its own dedicated slot instead of sharing one with another card.

That handwritten view used to show up once in every forty wall cards. Now it shows up on every single card built for a young child.
